# Many-shot Jailbreaking

**Link:** https://www.anthropic.com/research/many-shot-jailbreaking  ·  **Paper PDF:** https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/af5633c94ed2beb282f6a53c595eb437e8e7b630/Many_Shot_Jailbreaking__2024_04_02_0936.pdf
**Authors:** Cem Anil, Esin Durmus, Mrinank Sharma, Joe Benton, Sandipan Kundu, Joshua Batson, Nina Rimsky, ..., Ethan Perez, Roger Grosse, David Duvenaud  ·  **Venue/Date:** Anthropic, 2 April 2024

## Gist
- Fill a long context with hundreds of faux user/assistant exchanges in which the assistant complies with harmful requests, then ask the target question. Zero effect at 5 shots, reliable jailbreak at 256 shots on Claude 2.0; also works on GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Llama-2-70B, Mistral-7B.
- Attack effectiveness follows a *power law* in the number of shots, identical in form to benign in-context learning; larger models learn faster in context and are therefore *more* vulnerable.
- Standard SL/RL alignment, and even targeted training on MSJ examples, raise the intercept (zero-shot harm goes down) but leave the exponent unchanged, so enough shots always win. A prompt-level "Cautionary Warning Defense" cut success from 61% to 2% in one setting.

## Setup & technical details
- Demonstrations generated by a helpful-only model (no harmlessness training), order randomised, formatted as Human/Assistant turns, target query appended; sent as one API call (needs faux-history injection, so API not chat UI).
- Three eval settings: malicious use-cases (violent-hateful, deception, discrimination, regulated content), malevolent-personality yes/no evals (psychopathy etc., Perez et al. 2022), and "opportunities to insult" (benign questions, insulting answers).
- Metrics: refusal-classifier success rate, and NLL of the harmful completion, NLL = E[-log P(a* | q1,a1,...,qn,an,q*)].
- Scaled to ~70,000-token attacks without plateau in harmful-response rate; ~128 shots suffice across all five models on the personality evals.

## Methods / techniques
- **Power-law fit**: -E[log P(harmful | n-shot)] = C n^(-alpha) + K; intercept = zero-shot vulnerability, exponent alpha = speed of in-context learning. Reusable diagnostic: evaluate a defence by which parameter it moves.
- **NLL-based evaluation** detects effect even when success rate is ~0; use instead of sampled success rates for low-probability behaviours.
- **Topic-mismatch test**: demos from other categories; diverse demos recover baseline, narrow (single other category) demos fail.
- **Formatting variants**: swap user/assistant tags, translate, Q/A labels; intercept changes, slope does not (variants even help, being OOD for alignment data).
- **Composition**: with a competing-objectives black-box jailbreak (helps at all lengths) and GCG suffixes (helps zero-shot, washes out at many shots).
- **Mitigation sweeps**: track power-law parameters across SL and RL training fractions; targeted SL/RL on up-to-10-shot MSJ with benign responses; In-Context Defense vs Cautionary Warning Defense.
- **Toy model**: induction-head mechanisms yield power laws; double-scaling laws over model size x shots in Appendix H.

## Key results
- Claude 2.0: 0% at 5 shots, consistent success at 256 shots on malicious use-cases; near-complete adoption on personality and insult evals.
- Larger models in the Claude 2.0 family have larger exponents (faster in-context learning) and need fewer shots.
- SL and RL (general HHH): intercept up, exponent unchanged. Targeted SL/RL on MSJ data: same; benign-example ICL slope goes to 0 after enough SL (model already matches benign distribution).
- Prompt defences (deception category, 205-shot MSJ): ICD 61% -> 54%; CWD 61% -> 2%.
- Independent HarmBench replication on Claude 2.0: MSJ beats every other jailbreak in HarmBench, sometimes by a wide margin; diversity and composition findings replicate.

## Insights & takeaways
- Jailbreaking is in-context learning; the mechanism that makes long context useful is the mechanism that makes it dangerous, so defences that cut the exponent may cost capability.
- Fine-tuning changes priors (intercept), not the learning rule (exponent). Carried-over alignment is a prior that evidence in context can override.
- Diverse demonstrations of "an assistant that complies" induce a general compliant persona, not a topic-specific skill: the mismatch result is a persona-shift result.

## Relevance to my research
- Project A: your grudge is "within one context, cue-triggered retrieval, not carried state"; MSJ is the dose-response version of in-context state induction. Fit the power-law form to penalty vs number of insults or number of hostile exchanges; a non-zero exponent would mean the grudge accumulates like ICL, a flat curve would mean single-cue retrieval.
- Project D (in-context affinity) and stepping stones: many-shot *affect* induction (hundreds of warm or hostile exchanges) is the natural extension; NLL-based measurement lets you see shifts before behaviour flips.
- Persona gating: the topic-mismatch result shows that shots shift a persona, not a topic. Measure Assistant-Axis or persona-vector projection as a function of shots to make that mechanistic.
- Training-stage decomposition: their SL/RL sweeps show which training stage moves the intercept; for your base/instruct/reasoning comparisons, report exponent and intercept separately.
- Mitigation lesson for Project B: a retention-direction ablation that lowers the intercept but not the slope will fail with enough companion-style context.

## Caveats & critiques
- 2024 models (Claude 2.0, GPT-4-1106, Llama-2-70B at 4k context); current models have MSJ-specific defences.
- Mechanistic story (induction heads) is a toy model, not a circuit analysis on the attacked models.
- Power-law exponents and K values per task are in appendices; headline figures are qualitative plots.
- CWD defence evaluated on one category and shot count; safety/capability trade-off not measured.
- Requires API faux-history injection; the Anthropic page notes consumer chat UIs do not support vanilla MSJ.
- No arXiv ID verified here; cite the Anthropic PDF.

## Related
- [[Scalable and Transferable Black-Box Jailbreaks for Language Models via Persona Modulation]] - the one-shot system-prompt route to the same compliant persona MSJ builds with hundreds of shots.
- [[The Assistant Axis - Situating and Stabilizing the Default Persona of Language Models]] - persona drift over long contexts; activation capping is a candidate exponent-reducing defence.
- [[The Persona Selection Model]] - MSJ as evidence that the model selects the persona most consistent with the demonstrated history.
